mercy_translation.text:
The way of death is this. First of all, it is evil and full of curse: murders, adulteries, lusts, sexual immoralities, thefts, idolatries, magical practices, sorceries, robberies, false testimonies, hypocrisies, double-heartedness, deceit, arrogance, wickedness, self-will, greed, foul speech, jealousy, boldness, pride, and boastfulness.

They are persecutors of the good, haters of truth, lovers of falsehood, ignorant of the reward of righteousness, not clinging to what is good or to just judgment, keeping watch not for good but for evil. Meekness and patience are far from them. They love vain things, pursue repayment, show no mercy to the poor, do not labor for the afflicted, do not know the One who made them, are murderers of children and destroyers of God's creation, turn away from the needy, oppress the distressed, flatter the rich, judge the poor unlawfully, and are sinners in every way.

Children, may you be delivered from all these things.

translator_notes: Direct Mercy translation from the Greek public-domain source.
The chapter contrasts the Way of Death with the Way of Life and collects vices in catalogue form.
